chapter_theme: The old woman's instruction to the golden girl, and the end of the kalivenba: a rule for whom the awakened one should receive. Veda-and-Purana men bowing for show, pretenders of chariyai, wretched performers of kiriyai, fools who do not seek, the deceitful, shastra-paupers, the cotton-wads of gotra, book-ghosts, hatha-yoga idlers, left-hand adepts of Kama's text, name-dropping boasters, the mind-proud, sect-virtue gangs and kings of sham silence are all to be turned away; only the ancients of Siva-yoga and the owners of tapas, knowledge and silence are to be called in and told the Siva-substance, and the one who seeks the substance of knowledge is to be joined with grace.
structure_note: 2220 opens the address (listen, firm intellect); 2221 to 2222 set the scene at the gem-gate of turiya; 2223 to 2226 give the four paths, chariyai and kiriyai refused, yoga and jnana admitted; 2227 to 2233 list the kinds to refuse; 2234 closes the poem with the one to seek. The last unit is a single line, the natural close of a kalivenba.

2220.reading: 'Lightning, gold of the mind-lotus where nectar grew, listen with firm understanding': the old woman opens her instruction, and the rare-to-tell (2221) Veda-men she names first.
2220.nuance: The addressee is the girl of 2210 to 2219, so the instruction is Shakti's to the awakened soul; மனக்கமலப் பொன்னே, gold of the mind's lotus, makes her the thing that grew in the heart-lotus of 2150. The teaching that follows is about discernment of company, not about method.

2221.reading: Men of Veda and Purana will bow to your lotus feet out of empty show; do not look them in the face; and in nada (2222) at the gate of turiya appear.
2221.nuance: வெறும்பிலுக்கு, empty display: the scriptural men are not refused for error but for show. The awakened one is told to refuse even their homage, which inverts the usual order where the Vedic man is the honoured one.

2222.reading: Appear at the gem-gate of turiya in nada, show your face in the open so that you are truly known, and then go inside, rarely; and (2223) the chariyai-men who proclaim.
2222.nuance: துரியமணி வாசல், the gem-door of turiya, is read by tradition as the opening at the crown where the fourth state is entered; the awakened one shows herself there to be known and then withdraws within. முகம் சத்தே தெரிய is uncertain: 'so the face is truly seen' or 'the face in true being'. The plain image is of a woman at a doorway choosing whom to admit.

2223.reading: The chariyai-men who proclaim, swelling with pride, will praise you to embrace you; do not go after them; and the praised (2224) kiriyai-fools.
2223.nuance: சளுக்கர் is the proud, the puffed up; the first of the four Saiva paths, outward service, is here a pretension. The poem does not reject chariyai as such but those who make a show of it, the same charge as 2221.

2224.reading: The wretched performers of kiriyai, the fools, will worry to reach your form; pass them by; and the Siva-yoga (2225) ancients admit.
2224.nuance: அசடர், dolts: ritual worship, the second path, is given to fools. கடத்தி, convey past: they are not to be fought but set aside. 2225 then names the third path, yoga, as the first to be welcomed, so the four paths are graded by whom to let in.

2225.reading: If the ancients of Siva-yoga come and prostrate before your flower-feet, call them inside without wavering and speak with them; and the first (2226) tapas-jnana-silence masters.
2225.nuance: The yogis are received as equals in speech, பேசிக்கொள்; the jnanis of 2226 are to be told the Siva-substance. The awakened one is a hostess choosing guests, the Siddhar inversion of the disciple who seeks a teacher.

2226.reading: If the owners of the first tapas, knowledge and silence come, do not shame them; call them and tell them the Siva-substance; and the (2227) fools who do not seek.
2226.nuance: அவமானம் பண்ணாது: the only ones the girl might wrong by refusal are the silent knowers, so the instruction guards against the awakened one's own pride. சிவபொருள், the Siva-substance, is what is to be shared, and only with them.

2227.reading: Do not get caught by the fools who do not seek the Siva-substance; do not cling to the deceitful who do not seek in thought; and the unbending (2228) shastra-paupers.
2227.nuance: Two kinds are refused: fools who never seek and the deceitful who do not seek in the mind though they may in word; the test is inward seeking, not profession.

2228.reading: Do not go near the shastra-paupers who do not bend; do not join the cotton-wads of gotra who argue; and the sutra- (2229) liars.
2228.nuance: தூரித்தர் is read as தரித்திரர், paupers, those poor in everything but shastra; கோத்திரப் பஞ்சியளை, the cotton-wads of lineage, mocks those stuffed with gotra pride as cotton is stuffed; the word may also be பஞ்சையர், the destitute. தக்கமிடும் (arguing, bragging) qualifies them. சூத்திரப் carries into 2229.

2229.reading: Do not take to the desire of lying idlers of the sutras; do not want the desire of the book-ghosts, the true idlers; and the hatha-yoga (2230) men learned in Kama's text.
2229.nuance: புத்தகப்பேய், the book-ghost, is the strongest phrase of the chapter: one possessed by books. பொய்வீணர் and மெய்வீணர், false idlers and true idlers, seem to be a pair, the frauds and the sincerely useless; the second may also mean idlers about the body (மெய்). கையோகக் carries into 2230.

2230.reading: Do not set your mind on the left-hand adepts of hatha yoga who have learned the text of Kama's arts, made for lust; and those who set up a name (2231) and babble.
2230.nuance: கையோகம் (hand-yoga) is read as hatha yoga, the physical practice; வாமத்தார் are the left-hand tantrics, whose texts the poem calls Kama's book made for lust. The attack separates the Siddhars' breath-yoga from sexual tantra, a line not every Siddhar text draws.

2231.reading: If the show-offs of mossy station who parade under a name come, push them away so that their hearts burn, and do not stand; and (2232) do not go to the mind-proud.
2231.nuance: பாசிப் பதப் பிலுக்கர் is unclear; பாசி may be moss or a bead-string, so 'the show-offs of the bead-string station', wearers of rosaries for display. நாமமிட்டு may be taking a religious name or wearing the sect-mark called நாமம். நெஞ்செரிய, so their hearts burn: the only refusal told to be cruel.

2232.reading: Do not go where the proud of mind are; do not aim at the desire of the man who gathers sect-virtue; and the detached (2233) kings of sham silence.
2232.nuance: சீலமதக் கொத்தவன், he who bunches virtue by sect, is one whose morality is a badge of his faith. பற்றற்ற, detached, carries into 2233 as an ironic epithet for the silent rogues.

2233.reading: If the mischievous kings of silence, who claim detachment, fall for you, send them off in the manner that fits them; and the one who seeks the substance of knowledge (2234) join.
2233.nuance: மோனக் குறும்பரசர், kings of silence-mischief: men whose silence is a pose, matching the குறும்பு of anger, mind and recitation in 2185 to 2186. Against them 2226's owners of true silence are to be admitted, so silence itself is not the test; its honesty is.

2234.reading: Praising the able ones who seek the substance of knowledge, join them and go with grace: the poem's last word to the awakened one.
2234.nuance: The kalivenba ends on its single-line close with the one positive command after a dozen refusals: the company to keep is those who seek ஞானப்பொருள், and the going is அருளோடு, with grace, which the whole poem has made the guru's gift.

links.note: The Kural says hiding in austerity and doing what is not austerity is a hunter snaring birds from a bush; Thirikonar's chariyai-men praise the awakened one in order to embrace her, outward service as a cover for desire. Both expose the garb of religion used for gain.

The Naladiyar separates those who fill a house with books from those who understand them; Thirikonar's book-ghosts are the first kind, possessed by books, and the awakened one is told not to want their company.

Sivavakkiyar says the shastras recited and the books tied in bundles ended as nothing once he knew the Lord; Thirikonar's old woman tells the awakened girl to refuse the book-ghosts. Both set realised knowledge against text, though Thirikonar's girl has first mastered the southern and northern books (2215).

Tirumular says the three lower paths come naturally to those who reach sanmarga and the scriptures accept them as the path of the word; Thirikonar's old woman has the awakened one pass by the performers of kiriyai as fools and refuse the chariyai-men. The conflict holds if 2223 to 2224 reject the paths themselves and not only their proud practitioners; on the narrower reading, both could stand.

Tirumular says the garb is useless to those of petty knowledge and the good attain grace without it; Thirikonar's kings of sham silence, who claim detachment, are to be sent away while the true owners of silence (2226) are told the Siva-substance. Both judge the pose by the knowledge behind it.

source_issues: 2234 (thirikonar:91) has a single line, which is the normal close of a kalivenba and not a loss.
2228 தூரித்தர் and பஞ்சியளை, and 2231 பாசிப் பதப்பிலுக்கர், are unclear words, probably corrupt or dialectal.
